newsitem.title: GERMANY: Duisenberg not worried by dollar's recent rise.
newsitem.headline: Duisenberg not worried by dollar's recent rise.

text.p: Wim Duisenberg, the president-designate of the European Monetary Institute, said that he was not worried by the dollar's recent sharp rise, a German newspaper reported on Tuesday.
In an interview with the business daily Boersen-Zeitung, Duisenberg, head of the Dutch central bank, was quoted as saying he had "no problems" with the dollar's rise.

The fundamental stability of exchange rates, and expectations for exchange rates to remain stable, were more important than the dollar's actual levels, Duisenberg said. He added that economic decisions were based on these expectations.
Industry, in particular, needed to have an assurance that exchange rates between the dollar, the mark, the franc and others remain stable, Duisenberg told the newspaper.
The dollar has risen sharply in recent weeks and is currently trading around 1.64 marks.

Duisenberg, however, dismissed talk that squabbling over various issues concerning Europe's monetary union triggered the dollar's sharp rise, arguing this had begun even before political battles became public.
Debate about which nation will head the European Central bank and talk about a possible additional stability council could not have impacted currency rates very much, Duisenberg said.
European nations are at odds over the nationality of the future president of the central bank with several German officials saying the post should not be held by France.
Duisenberg said he would be eager to take on the position but stressed that no final decision had been taken on the matter.
